source.title: Joint Training Across Multiple Activation Sparsity Regimes

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether an activation constraint changes test performance, using a training intervention and test accuracy rather than the claim versions’ specified methods or measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports CIFAR-10 test accuracy for a dense baseline and two activation-sparsity training strategies. It does not report training error, the train–test gap, random-label fitting, or any of the specific interventions or measurements in V1–V8. Cited results in the introduction are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study cites random-label memorization as motivation but tests activation-sparsity cycling, which none of V1–V8 names. Its own results do not test or operationally use any claim version. Top-k activation suppression is not a dropout comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: both controllers improved best test accuracy over the dense baseline in single-run CIFAR-10 experiments without augmentation. The authors characterize the findings as preliminary and call for repeated runs and broader validation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses top-k activation constraints with adaptive compression and periodic reset; the study does not test the original sources’ methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The two keep-ratio controllers produced different reported best test accuracies and peak epochs; only single runs were conducted.

fits_no_version.finding: In single runs on CIFAR-10 without augmentation, best test accuracy was 86.90% for dense training, 87.97% for Strategy 1, and 88.02% for Strategy 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cycling a WRN-28-4 through top-k activation budgets can improve best test accuracy over dense training under this recipe; replication is needed.

record.problems: Single-run experiments; hyperparameters were not systematically optimized; no reported uncertainty; no training-error or train–test-gap results; experiments cover one architecture and one dataset.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to interpolate.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under different tuning and recovery recipes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce their penalty.
Dropout effects and their dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, augmentation, and weight decay. No dropout is used.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text omits the plotted contents of Figures 1–3, so it cannot establish that training-accuracy curves are absent from the paper. Neither training accuracy nor a train–test gap alone would make this intervention a test of V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization alongside it, and the specified architectures.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and local-connectivity effects.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning conditions.
Large- versus small-batch comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to batch size.
Dropout comparisons and its interaction with training-set size, data augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.

rows.subject: WRN-28-4 dense baseline
rows.operation_detail: Dense baseline training without additional activation compression.
rows.note: The study does not provide training accuracy or error for comparison, so this result cannot establish a train–test gap.
rows.check: The baseline accuracy of 0.869 is correctly transcribed, but standalone test accuracy bears on none of V1–V8.

rows.subject: WRN-28-4, Strategy 1
rows.operation_detail: Training with top-k activation sparsity and additive compression with local drop-triggered reset.

conditions.value: additive step of 0.01; reset when smoothed training accuracy decreases by 0.01

rows.note: Test accuracy exceeds the dense baseline, but the study does not report training error or the train–test gap.
rows.check: The accuracy of 0.8797 versus 0.869 is correctly transcribed. This is the study's own activation-sparsity method comparison, not evidence for any listed version; retain only as a finding outside those versions.

rows.subject: WRN-28-4, Strategy 2
rows.operation_detail: Training with top-k activation sparsity and multiplicative compression with best-gap-triggered reset.

conditions.value: multiplicative decay of 0.98; reset when smoothed training accuracy falls more than 0.2 below its best historical value

rows.note: Test accuracy exceeds the dense baseline, but the study does not report training error or the train–test gap.
rows.check: The accuracy of 0.8802 versus 0.869 is correctly transcribed. This is the study's own activation-sparsity method comparison, not evidence for any listed version; retain only as a finding outside those versions.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
